newsitem.title: THAILAND: Star Petroleum says reviewing condensate project.
newsitem.headline: Star Petroleum says reviewing condensate project.

text.p: Star Petroleum Refining Co (SPRC), a Caltex Petroleum Corp unit, said it is reviewing whether or not to go ahead with a plan to build a 600,000 tonnes per year condensate splitter.
SPRC managing director Don Romano said in a statement to Reuters that the company was conducting a feasibility study and will make a decision by mid-1997.
He also denied a local media report that the delay was caused by financial problems.
"SPRC is looking seriously at the possibility of constructing a condensate splitter as an addition to the current refining capacity," he said.
"It is currently conducting a number of studies that are looking at the economic feasibility of such investment, taking into account projected condensate prices and construction costs," he added.
SPRC currently runs a 145,000-barrels-per-day refinery in the eastern province of Rayong.
Caltex holds a 64 percent stake in SPRC with state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand owning the rest. Caltex is a joint venture of U.S. majors Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
